title: Less Stringent Criteria for Rental and Purchase of HDB Flats for Families Affected by Divorce or With School-going Children
what_it_is: Less Stringent Criteria for Rental and Purchase of HDB Flats for Families Affected by Divorce or With School-going Children

sections.label: Rental flat income ceiling and priority
sections.summary: The $1,500 income ceiling prioritises rental flats for low-income households, while HDB allows flexibility, priority allocation and reduced waiting times.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: At $1,500 per month of income, the current income ceiling enables us to prioritise our rental flat supply for low-income households.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, the Housing and Development Board (HDB) exercises flexibility to allow some families with higher income to get a public rental flat, if they have no family support and no other viable housing options.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: HDB also grants priority allocation of rental flats on a case-by-case basis to families with school-going children, for example, to accommodate arrangements for the care of these children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Even without priority allocation, the waiting time for a rental flat has been reduced substantially from 21 months in 2008 to four months in 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: For Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) exercises, HDB already gives priority to families with children through the Third Child Priority Scheme (TCPS) as well as the Parenthood Priority Scheme (PPS).
